explanation: Port = carry, -able = able to be. Portable means easy to carry, like a portable speaker. 'Imported' shares the root (carried in from another country) but means something else. Tip: 'port' words move things (transport, export).
Aud = hear, -ible = able to be. Audible means loud enough to be heard. 'Visible' has the same ending but 'vis' = see. Tip: 'aud' words are about hearing (audio, audience).
Trans = through or across, par = appear. Transparent means you can see through it, like glass. 'Carried across' is the trans- trap. Tip: if light 'appears through' it, it's transparent.
De = remove, hydr = water. To dehydrate is to remove water, or dry out. 'Soak' is the opposite trap. Tip: 'hydr' words are watery (hydrant, hydrate).

Bio = life, graph = write. A biography is the written story of a real person's life. 'Made-up tale' is the opposite trap, since a biography is true. Tip: 'graph' words involve writing or drawing (autograph, paragraph).

Magn = great or large, -ify = make. To magnify is to make bigger. 'Attract' is a magnet trap, and 'examine' is what you might do with a magnifying glass. Tip: 'magn' words are big (magnitude, magnificent).
Aqua = water. Aquatic animals live in water, like fish and dolphins. 'Sky-blue' is the aquamarine trap. Tip: 'aqua' words are watery (aquarium, aqueduct).

Spect = look, -or = a person who. A spectator is a person who watches, like the fans at Camp Nou. 'Player' is the opposite trap, and 'inspector' shares the root but means someone who checks things. Tip: 'spect' words involve looking (spectacles, inspect).
Bene = good, fact = do or make. A benefactor does good for others: a helper or supporter. 'Enemy' is the opposite trap. Tip: 'bene-' words are positive.

Mal = bad, vol = wish. Malevolent means wishing harm on others, like a movie villain. 'Kindhearted' is the opposite trap, and 'sickly' borrows the 'mal' from malady. Tip: 'mal-' words are negative (malfunction, malice).

Chron = time. Something chronic lasts a long time or keeps coming back, like a chronic cough. 'Brief' is the opposite trap, and 'colorful' is a sound-alike (chrome). 'Painful' is tempting because people say 'chronic pain'. Tip: 'chron' words are about time (chronological).

Omni = all, potent = powerful. Omnipotent means having unlimited power. 'All-knowing' shares the root but is omniscient. 'Helpless' is the opposite trap. Tip: 'omni' means all (omnivore eats everything).

Mono = one, ton = tone. Something monotonous stays on one tone, so it is boring and repetitive. 'Exciting' is the opposite trap, and 'single-colored' is a mono- trap (that's monochrome). Tip: 'mono' means one (monologue).

Sub = under, terr = earth. Subterranean means under the earth, like a subway tunnel. 'Airborne' is the opposite trap, and 'territorial' shares the root but means protective of land. Tip: 'sub-' means under (submarine).

Phil = love, anthrop = humankind. A philanthropist loves people and gives money to help them. A people-hater is the opposite (a misanthrope), and a stamp collector is a philatelist, which shares the root 'phil'. Tip: 'phil' means love (Philadelphia = brotherly love).

Re = back, voc = call. To revoke is to call back, or cancel, like revoking a red card after video review. 'Grant' is the opposite trap, 'shout' shares the voice root (vocal), and 'revive' just sounds similar. Tip: 'voc' means voice or call.

Am = love or friend, -able = able to be. Amiable means friendly and easy to like. 'Unfriendly' is the opposite trap, and 'amusing' just sounds similar. Tip: 'am' words are about love and friendship (amicable, amigo).

Fid = faith or trust. Fidelity means staying faithful, or loyalty, like a fan who sticks with the club in bad seasons. 'Betrayal' is the opposite trap, and 'restlessness' is a fidget sound-alike. Tip: 'fid' words involve trust (confident).

Pac = peace, -ify = make. To pacify is to make peaceful, or calm someone down. 'Provoke' is the opposite trap; 'pack' and 'specify' only sound alike. Tip: the Pacific Ocean was named the 'peaceful' ocean.

Contra = against, dict = say. To contradict is to say the opposite, or deny. 'Confirm' is the opposite trap, and 'dictate' shares the root but means to say something for someone to write down. 'Shrink' is a contract sound-alike. Tip: 'dict' means say (dictionary).

Ped = foot. A pedestrian travels on foot: a walker. 'Driver' is the opposite trap, and a children's doctor (pediatrician) looks similar but comes from a different Greek 'ped' that means child. Tip: 'ped' words often involve feet (pedal).

Post = after, pon = put. To postpone is to put something off until after, like a match postponed by a storm. 'Hurry' is the opposite trap, and 'mail' is a 'post' sound trap. Tip: 'post-' means after (postgame).

Circum = around, spect = look. A circumspect person looks all around before acting: cautious. 'Careless' is the opposite trap, 'round' is the circum trap, and 'suspicious' shares the 'spect' root but means distrustful. Tip: break long words into parts.

In = not, cred = believe. Incredulous means not able to believe something. 'Trusting' is the opposite trap, and 'amazing' comes from 'incredible', which describes the thing, not the person. Tip: incredulous people react to incredible things.

Poly = many, glot = tongue or language. A polyglot speaks many languages, like many Barca players who speak Spanish, Catalan and English. A many-sided shape is a polygon, which shares 'poly'. Tip: 'poly' means many.

Trans = across, -ient comes from ire = go. Something transient passes by quickly, so it's fleeting or temporary. 'Lasting' is the opposite trap, and 'transparent' shares the 'trans' prefix. Tip: transient things are just passing through.

Loqu = speak, -acious = full of. A loquacious person is full of talk: talkative. 'Quiet' is the opposite trap, and 'well-spoken' (eloquent) shares the root but is about speaking well, not a lot. Tip: 'loqu' words involve speech (eloquent, colloquial).
Ver = true. Veracity means truthfulness. 'Dishonesty' is the opposite trap; 'speed' (velocity) and 'hunger' (voracity) are sound-alikes. Tip: 'ver' words are about truth (verify, verdict).

Ante = before, ced = go. An antecedent goes before something else. 'A result' is the opposite trap; 'a funny story' (anecdote) and 'a remedy' (antidote) are sound-alikes. Tip: 'ante-' means before, 'anti-' means against.

Intra = within, mur = wall. Intramural sports happen within the walls of one school, like a class-vs-class soccer league. 'Between schools' is the inter- trap, and 'painted on walls' is the mural trap. Tip: intra = inside, inter = between.
